alt: Editorial plate: a floodlit night at Anfield, a midfielder in red striking a volley from thirty yards, the ball leaving his boot in a blur, a goalkeeper in the distance beginning to move the wrong way, a wall of supporters rising behind the goal.
focus: Carried plate, not this edition's lead. The Szoboszlai volley from Liverpool 3-1 Tottenham, Carabao Cup third round, 15 September, remains the season's most recent photographable moment while the front page leads on a Saturday that moved the table around a club which did not play in it.
leadStory: Five Premier League matches were completed on Saturday 19 September while Liverpool trained and travelled to Dorset, and every one of them moved the table. Brighton beat Arsenal 3-0 at the Amex, through Pascal Gross on 31, Charalampos Kostoulas on 45 and Chema Andres heading in a corner just before the hour on his first Premier League start, ending the champions' perfect start and their pursuit of a 123-year club record of eight straight wins to open a season; Everton beat Ipswich 1-0; Newcastle beat Hull 2-1 to inflict a promoted side's first defeat; Coventry won 1-0 at Nottingham Forest for their first points and first goal of the season in the same afternoon; and Tottenham scored their first league goals of the campaign and lost 3-2 to Aston Villa anyway. Liverpool fell from eighth to tenth on the same six points from four, three points behind both the Champions League line (Brentford, fourth) and the Europa line (Everton, fifth), with a game in hand on every club from second to ninth bar Leeds. That game is Bournemouth away at 2pm on Sunday 20 September, Andoni Iraola's first return to the club he managed for three years and left in June. Liverpool also confirmed two October dates: Chelsea at Anfield in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday 28 October, and the Champions League trip to LASK in Linz on Wednesday 14 October.
